title: Umbraflow ProjectRegistrationManifest v4
$comment: The one-closure registration. A generation carries the tool closure compiled on the scoped program type, with its own module manifest hash and its own stated export surface. There is ONE reader and it accepts project_registration_format 7 and refuses everything else, so the format integer is an identity assertion inside a reader and never a key anything dispatches on. Format 7 is format 6 without reducer_closure, project_state_schema_hash, project_tool_precondition_schema_hash, journal_event_schema_manifest_hash and baseline_event_type: the framework stopped interpreting a Project's state, so the fold, the documents it folded and the family they belonged to have no reader left, and a pinned document nothing judges is the defect.

project_registration_format.$comment: The generation of this registration contract a framework must understand, not the bytes of the file that states it. Editing this schema's prose is not a new generation and must not move the registration root of a project already published against it.

tool_closure.$comment: The closure compiled on the scoped program type, and the only closure a generation carries. Its exported_entry_points is exactly the union of project_tool_bindings' entry points. The slot is required and stays required: a project that binds no Tool ships this closure with an empty exported_entry_points and an empty project_tool_bindings, because explicit emptiness is a value and an optional slot would be an absence carrying a meaning.

tool_catalog_hash.$comment: The sha256 of the exact canonical bytes of the Tool declarations this registration pins. There is no Tool Catalog document and no catalog file: the deployment states its Tools inline, the loader renders them canonically, and this is the digest of those bytes. Every bound a call is judged against is inside it, so a widened bound moves this hash and therefore project_registration_hash.

observed_instance_identity_schema_hashes.$comment: The closed set of observed-instance identity schema documents this registration owns, as the sha256 of each document's exact canonical bytes. The deployment states the documents inline and the loader derives every digest from the bytes it read, sorted and unique by that derivation -- JSON Schema cannot state sortedness, so the framework's own reading of the derived document refuses any other order.

project_resources.$comment: The one resource closure a registration pins. A registration pins the bytes a project registered once, and those bytes are the opaque supply the scoped program is compiled over.

project_tool_bindings.$comment: The Project Tool binding table: one row per Tool this registration binds to an entry point of the tool closure. It sits beside tool_catalog_hash rather than inside the declarations because a binding is the join of a contract name and a code entry, and a declaration carrying it could no longer be served to a caller and verified against the pinned digest. It is inside this root because a re-registration that rebound a Tool to different code without moving project_registration_hash would leave the pinned environment no longer pinning which code answers a call. Sorted and unique by tool_name -- JSON Schema cannot state sortedness, so the framework's own reading refuses any other order. An empty array is a registration that binds no Tool.

closure.$comment: The compiled closure of a generation. Both members are required in every version of this contract: exported_entry_points is what the authoring path observed the closure to offer, and a version of this schema without it would teach a reader that an absent statement means an unchecked one -- the exact absent-means-something reading the join exists to refuse. The declaration is the entry points only; plugin_id is a field of every closure and is never named here, so an empty array is the whole statement that a closure offers no entry point.
